mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals strengthening economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances following a 3-month GDP increase, or the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in industrial production signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates a slowdown in economic activity and potential earnings declines.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances following a 3-month decline in industrial production, or the correlation between industrial production decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and retail sales signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors benefit.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint correlation between housing starts, retail sales increase, and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it indicates a potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between nonfarm payroll decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between CPI increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in both real GDP and housing starts signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as broad-based economic growth supports corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint correlation between GDP, housing starts increase, and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
